submission.justification: Provisional recommendation only. Radiator-R2 at 4 cm gives the highest simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c of all candidates and thicknesses tested (4.554 sigma; R2 at 3 cm gives 4.477 and at 2 cm gives 4.498). However, the hard transparency constraint is NOT verified. No ageing data were found in the project documents for any of the three candidates (candidates_with_ageing_data = 0, ageing loss recorded as -1/unknown), so eligible_candidates_count = 0. I cannot confirm that R2 at 4 cm keeps transparency loss at or below 10% after the 10-year-equivalent humidity test. Because the radiator cannot be replaced during the run, this choice should not be treated as final until a humidity ageing test for R2 shows loss of 10% or less. If R2 fails that test, the next choice would need to be re-evaluated against the ageing results for R1 and R3, which are also unverified. The separation advantage of R2 over the other candidates is about 0.5 to 1.4 sigma, but that advantage does not override the hard ageing requirement.
